The page 18 example caption describes the pictured heavy-impact tapered-bearing outer-ring indentations as true metal deformation, not wear as with false brinelling, and notes that grinding marks are still visible in the groove [EV-K01-004]. The supplied CWT/category input (predicted_class 'outer_race') cannot establish which texture is physically present here: it is a caller-assigned class with no actual classifier or task-model inference, and the scenario's assumed cause (external vibration during standstill) is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation [EV-K01-001]. The texture cue is a qualitative physical-surface inspection of the actual depression or wear area, and no quantitative threshold is supplied [EV-K01-004].

Evidence limitations:
The texture comparison is a qualitative physical-surface inspection cue requiring examination of the actual depression or wear area; no quantitative decision threshold is provided [EV-K01-004].

The NSK outer-ring false-brinelling example is a manufacturer case for a deep-groove ball bearing attributed to external vibration while stationary; it does not show that all outer-ring faults share this mechanism or that any project sample has this condition [EV-K01-001].
The supplied class/category input is a caller-assigned label, not a classifier or task-model result, and the assumed cause is a teaching assumption rather than an observed sample fact [EV-K01-001].
No actual device records, model-specific thresholds, or aviation/reuse authorization were supplied, so no damage cause, maintenance parameter, reuse, or aircraft-release conclusion can be drawn.
